items.title: US Fed holds interest rates steady despite 'too high' inflation

items.summary: The 12-member Federal Open Market Committee voted 10-2 to hold rates at a target range between 3.75 to 4.00 percent, citing the need for more data in the fight against inflation, after having hiked for the first time in three years at its previous meeting in September.

items.title: Haze disrupts schooling, threatens learning outcomes

But in Central Kalimantan, one of the provinces hardest hit by forest and peatland fires this year, students will have to wait until next month to sit the exam because of deteriorating air quality.

items.title: Analysis: Pinpointing corporate culprits behind Indonesia’s wildfires

items.summary: As Indonesia continues to grapple with spreading wildfires and recurring haze, scrutiny has increasingly shifted toward corporate culpability, driven by investigative reports linking vast networks of foreign investors and multinational firms to the blazes. With Jakarta’s domestic response perceived as largely muted, neighboring ASEAN member states have begun mounting diplomatic pressure and pursuing independent investigations into the entities allegedly responsible for the transboundary haze choking the region.

The listing also elevated the RIL group to the top of India's most valued business houses. Jio’s IPO was oversubscribed more than 22 times, indicating strong investor interest.

items.title: Ronaldo beats Messi to win inaugural BOAT award for 2008 Man United season
items.title_zh: 罗纳尔多击败梅西赢得2008年曼联赛季的首届船奖
items.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo has been named the first-ever winner of the BOAT award for his 2008 season. Fans voted in a digital process that compared his performance to Lionel Messi's seasons. While Ronaldo's win added to his legacy, Messi occupied many top positions alongside him. More than 5,000 votes were cast, showcasing the high interest in this competition. The award highlights the ongoing rivalry between these two football legends in history.

items.title: Farmers claim Rs 35 cr missing from PNB FDs in Greater Noida; 5 suspended

Account holders have accused bank staff of embezzling approximately Rs 35 crore through unauthorized transactions. At least 16 account holders, primarily farmers, have filed complaints regarding the matter with local police. The bank has suspended five staff members, including the branch manager, while initiating an internal inquiry.

items.title: Sam Altman to MBA students: ‘Chronic disappointment’ that they chase old trends

items.summary: Sam Altman, CEO of OpenAI, expressed disappointment that MBA graduates pursue outdated career paths instead of embracing AI. He emphasized that AI presents transformative opportunities for ambitious workers and entrepreneurs. Altman believes that current technological changes facilitate the foundation of innovative companies that were once unattainable. Other tech leaders, like Mark Cuban, support the notion of integrating AI into business strategies.

The BJP secured six seats against the SP's five in the elections for 11 available constituencies. Among the graduates' and teachers' seats, significant victories were recorded by both parties. Independent candidates also made their mark by winning two teacher seats before joining the BJP and SP.

items.title: Meet Seiji Iigaya, 14: Python violin study wins $3,500 national science award

items.summary: Seiji Iigaya, a 14-year-old violinist from New Jersey, won the First Place Science Award at a national contest. He conducted research on how bow movements impact the tone of violin strings. Using programming, he modeled and analyzed the dynamics of a vibrating violin string. His study provided insights into achieving expressive sound without harshness. Seiji's school received a grant to support local STEM projects as part of the award.

items.title: PM says to foster 200 'frontier' bio, pharmaceutical firms by 2030
items.title_zh: 首相表示，到2030年将培育200家“前沿”生物制药公司
items.summary: Prime Minister Han Seong-sook said Thursday that the government will select 200 bio and pharmaceutical companies by 2030 and help them grow enough to compete on the global stage. Han made the remark at a national policy coordination meeting held at a Chong Kun Dang Pharmaceutical Corp. factory in the central city of Cheonan, stressing that Korea should identify and foster innovative firms armed with new technologies and ideas. She said 50 "frontier" companies will be selected every year by 2030 and the government will provide them with "support for research, development and investment at each stage of growth from the development of candidate substances to clinical trials and commercialization." The government plans to assign a dedicated director to each selected company to provide customized support for up to five years. It will also inject 150 billion won ($112 million) in policy financing over three years, comprising 60 billion won in investments through banks specializing in research and development (R&D) and 90 billion won in guarantees from the Korea Technology Finance Corporation.

items.title: Incheon Global Campus aims to become engine of regional innovation
items.title_zh: 仁川全球校区旨在成为区域创新的引擎
items.summary: Students seeking degrees from prestigious universities overseas could head straight to their main campuses overseas. But Incheon Global Campus (IGC) is making a case for choosing Korea instead, offering access to the country's thriving high-tech industries alongside a world-class education. Located in the Incheon Free Economic Zone (IFEZ), IGC is seeking to turn its proximity to major biotechnology, semiconductor and other advanced technology companies into a competitive advantage, connecting international education with hands-on industry experience and career opportunities. "Simply having prestigious foreign universities in Incheon is no longer enough to prove our value," said Byun Ju-young, CEO of the Incheon Global Campus Foundation, during an interview with The Korea Times. "What matters now is whether their education and research capabilities can translate into technological innovation and job creation in the region." items.title: Korea seeks 'top-down' approach with US for breakthrough in OPCON transfer
items.title_zh: 韩国寻求与美国“自上而下”的方法，在OPCON转移方面取得突破
items.summary: Korea will seek a "top-down" approach with the United States for a breakthrough in the wartime operational control (OPCON) transition, the defense ministry said Thursday, dismissing the view that a delay of the allies' annual security talks signals a setback in the transfer timeline. The allies announced Wednesday the Security Consultative Meeting (SCM), a key dialogue between their defense chiefs, has been pushed back to early next year, following bilateral talks between Defense Minister Kang Shin-chul and U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth in the Philippines earlier in the day. The ministry said Kang and Hegseth plan to meet again for another round of talks in Washington in December, viewed to be a rare move given that the SCM typically works "bottom-up" — bringing the defense chiefs together to finalize agreements reached during prior working-level consultations between their top military officers. items.title: Lee vows to leave no suspicions unresolved on 4th anniv. of Itaewon crowd crush
items.title_zh: 李发誓在梨泰院人群迷恋的四周年纪念日不会留下任何未解决的怀疑
items.summary: President Lee Jae Myung vowed Thursday to leave no suspicions unresolved regarding the deadly 2022 Itaewon crowd crush as he marked its fourth anniversary. Lee made the promise during a memorial event at Seoul's Gwanghwamun Square, which brought together some 1,000 people, including victims, bereaved family members and lawmakers. "I will make sure the people are never again sacrificed unjustly due to the state's absence and negligence," he said, alluding to the preceding administration of President Yoon Suk Yeol, which was in office at the time of the tragedy. "My administration is focusing the nation's capabilities on creating a country where everyone is safe," he added, citing new legislation aimed at better protecting people from disasters and accidents. Lee noted that under his administration the mandate of a special commission investigating the disaster has been extended until September 2027. "This is a promise to uncover the truth until not a single suspicion remains and ensure the truth leads to preventing a recurrence," he said. The tragedy happened on Oct. 29, 2022, during Hallowe

items.title: Overseas Koreans can now renew military discharge cards at embassies
items.title_zh: 海外韩国人现在可以在大使馆续签退伍卡
items.summary: Overseas Koreans living abroad can now easily apply for the reissuance of their military discharge certificates at Korean diplomatic missions, including embassies and consulates, without appointing a proxy in Korea. The Military Manpower Administration (MMA) and the Overseas Koreans Agency (OKA) announced Thursday that the expanded consular service takes effect immediately. Previously, diplomatic missions provided military service certificates, but lacked a system to issue replacement discharge certificates. Consequently, Koreans residing overseas who lost or damaged their certificates had to designate a representative back home to handle the application process, causing significant inconvenience. To honor veterans and streamline administrative support, the MMA issues wallet-sized, card-style discharge certificates in both Korean and English. Under the new arrangement, the MMA updated the relevant legal framework and established an integrated network with the OKA’s Consular Services 24 system. items.title: Cheong Wa Dae seeks fairer priority system for postpartum care centers
items.title_zh: Cheong Wa Dae为产后护理中心寻求更公平的优先制度
items.summary: Cheong Wa Dae said Thursday it will consider revising the law to ensure greater fairness and rationality in prioritizing access to postpartum care centers. Postpartum care centers, where new mothers stay and recover after childbirth, are popular in South Korea. Those subsidized by local governments, in particular, face intense competition for reservations because they charge relatively low fees. The issue drew media attention after President Lee Jae Myung shared an online community post on his X account Wednesday, which questioned whether mothers from multicultural families and mothers recognized as persons of national merit should be placed in the same second-priority category for reservations at Seoul-style postpartum care centers. Lee said the government would conduct an in-depth review, including consultations with local governments and possible legal amendments, to determine whether there is a compelling need to provide multicultural families with preferential treatment. items.title: K-water signs MOU with Austin to share AI water management technology
items.title_zh: K-water与奥斯汀签署谅解备忘录，分享人工智能水管理技术
items.summary: Korea Water Resources Corporation (K-water) signed a memorandum of understanding on Thursday with Austin, Texas, to cooperate on artificial intelligence (AI) water management, meeting with a delegation led by Michael Rogers, the city’s assistant city manager. The pact aims to share data-based smart water management solutions in response to the climate crisis and the growth of advanced industries, while strengthening a sustainable global water cooperation network. Key areas include sharing best practices and technologies, holding joint seminars to build smart water management capabilities, and identifying and implementing joint proof-of-concept projects for local application. Discussions began in January at CES 2026, when the Greater Austin Asian Chamber of Commerce expressed interest in K-water’s technologies. Following exchanges that included K-water’s August attendance at the Central Texas-Korea Summit, the Austin delegation’s Korea visit and the signing of the agreement have laid the groundwork for substantive cooperation. items.title: Special counsel again seeks death penalty for ex-President Yoon over martial law
items.title_zh: 特别顾问再次因戒严而寻求对前总统尹施行死刑
items.summary: A special counsel team on Thursday sought the death penalty for former President Yoon Suk Yeol during his appeal trial on insurrection charges stemming from his failed attempt to impose martial law. Special counsel Cho Eun-suk's team requested the sentence during proceedings at the Seoul High Court, eight months after a lower court sentenced Yoon to life imprisonment for staging a riot through his declaration of martial law on Dec. 3, 2024. "There is no reason to hesitate to hand down the death penalty," a member of the team said. "The strongest argument for objection to the death penalty is the possibility of a misjudgment just in case, but in this case, there is no room for that." Yoon declared martial law with the stated aim of eradicating anti-state forces, though the order was lifted six hours later by a vote by the National Assembly. During those six hours, troops were deployed to the National Assembly compound, which the lower court ruled in February was an attempt to paralyze parliament and arrest key politicians. items.title: Lee's approval rating rises to 46%: poll
items.title_zh: Lee的支持率上升至46 ％ ：民意调查
items.summary: President Lee Jae Myung's approval rating rose to 46 percent this week, surpassing his disapproval rating for the first time in nearly two months, a biweekly poll showed Thursday. In a survey of 1,000 adults nationwide conducted Monday through Wednesday, positive assessments of Lee's job performance rose 2 percentage points from two weeks earlier, according to the National Barometer Survey (NBS). Negative assessments fell 5 percentage points to 44 percent. Lee's approval rating last exceeded his disapproval rating in late August, when positive assessments stood at 50 percent. It then fell to a record low of 43 percent for two consecutive surveys in mid-September and the first week of October, before rising to 44 percent in the previous poll. Support for the ruling Democratic Party rose 3 percentage points to 36 percent, while that of the main opposition People Power Party fell 3 percentage points to 25 percent. items.title: Seoul arson suspect referred to prosecution for attempted murder

The suspect in his 70s, surnamed Lee, was taken into custody on Oct. 20 shortly after setting fires at two patent firms in two separate buildings in Seoul's Gangnam Ward. The blazes left 26 people injured, including a patent attorney, who suffered cardiac arrest. Lee claimed he had no intention of hurting anyone, but the Seoul Suseo Police Station sent the suspect to the Seoul Central District Prosecutors' Office on Thursday on charges of arson resulting in injuries and attempted murder, after concluding that the attack had been planned in advance with intent to cause the deaths of unspecified people According to police, Lee purchased two containers and two lighters between Sept. 24 and Oct. 5. items.summary: RIYADH — Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques King Salman and Crown Prince and Prime Minister Mohammed bin Salman offered condolences to King Felipe VI of Spain over the train collision tragedy that occurred in central Spain, resulting in multiple deaths and injuries. In separate cables sent to King Felipe, King Salman and the Crown Prince extended their deepest condolences and sincere sympathy to the Spanish king, the families of the deceased, and the Spanish people. They wished the injured a speedy recovery.

items.title: Tourism minister launches "Saudi Winter" events calendar
items.title_zh: 旅游部长推出“沙特冬季”活动日历
items.summary: RIYADH — Minister of Tourism Ahmed Al-Khateeb launched this year's Saudi Winter events calendar, featuring a wide range of tourism events and activities across several winter destinations in Saudi Arabia. The events under the theme “Saudi winter the way you love it” will be held in Riyadh, AlUla, Al-Qassim, Hail, Jeddah, Al-Khobar, Al-Ahsa, Madinah, and the Red Sea.The calendar offers visitors numerous options for enjoying a winter season filled with experiences catering to different interests and age groups.The launch provides visitors with a comprehensive guide to the major events, activities, and experiences available across Saudi destinations during the season, combining entertainment, culture, adventure, and relaxation. Offerings range from festivals, sporting events, live performances, and cultural and heritage experiences to nature excursions, desert adventures, and resort stays, alongside diverse dining, café, shopping, and seaside experiences. These options allow families and friends to tailor their trips to their interests and enjoy multiple experiences during a single visit.The Saudi Winter events calendar highlights the diversity of experiences offered by Saudi Arabia's winter destinations, from major international events and urban entertainment to historical sites, nature trails, and desert adventures, allowing visitors to choose their preferred experiences and discover more of what Saudi Arabia has to offer during the winter season.The Saudi Tourism Authority (STA) previously organized a workshop for this year's Saudi Winter program, bringing together more than 100 public and private sector partners. The program features over 1,800 tourism products, along with numerous distinctive events, activities, and cultural and nature-based experiences designed to appeal to diverse visitor segments, strengthen destination competitiveness, and enhance the attractiveness of Saudi destinations during the winter season.The events calendar is available on the ministry's official website.

items.title: Saudi, Malaysian, Kuwaiti defense ministers discuss regional developments in phone call
items.title_zh: 沙特、马来西亚、科威特国防部长在电话中讨论地区发展
items.summary: RIYADH — Saudi Minister of Defense Prince Khalid bin Salman held on Wednesday a phone call with Malaysian Minister of Defense Mohamed Khaled Nordin.During the call, the ministers discussed bilateral defense relations and reviewed regional developments. They also condemned the attacks launched by the terrorist Houthi militia against Saudi Arabia and the holy sites. Prince Khalid bin Salman also held a phone call with his Kuwaiti counterpart Sheikh Abdullah Ali Abdullah Al-Salem Al-Sabah. During the call, they reviewed the fraternal relations between the two countries in the defense field. The ministers discussed the latest developments in the region. They affirmed solidarity in confronting all challenges and threats so as to preserve the security and stability of both countries.

items.title: Saudi FM calls Spanish counterpart to offer condolences over deadly train crash
items.title_zh: 沙特调频致电西班牙同行，对致命的火车事故表示哀悼
items.summary: RIYADH — Minister of Foreign Affairs Prince Faisal bin Farhan held on Wednesday a phone call with Spanish Minister of Foreign Affairs, European Union and Cooperation José Manuel Albares. During the call, Prince Faisal extended Saudi Arabia's condolences to the government and people of Spain and to the families of the victims of the high-speed train collision in Toledo province. He expressed Saudi Arabia’s solidarity with Spain. The minister wished the injured a speedy recovery. At least 68 people died and more than 100 were injured when a Spanish high-speed express slammed into a stationary train on Wednesday, with rescuers scouring mangled carriages for more bodies after Spain's second fatal rail crash this year and Europe's deadliest since 2013.

items.title: Absher carries out 49 million transactions in September
items.title_zh: Absher在9月份进行了4900万笔交易
items.summary: MANAMA — The Ministry of Interior’s electronic platform Absher recorded more than 48.9 million electronic transactions in September 2026. This reaffirms Absher’s continued role in facilitating convenient and seamless access to digital services for citizens, residents, and visitors. The Absher Individuals platform accounted for 46,309,398 transactions, while the Absher Business platform recorded 2,600,152 transactions. The document-viewing service through the digital document wallet registered the highest usage, accounting for 37,580,936 transactions. Among the services delivered by the Ministry of Interior’s various sectors, the General Directorate of Public Security has processed 3,471,895 electronic transactions, including 3,339,579 transactions through the General Directorate of Traffic. The General Directorate of Passports handled 2,111,173 transactions, while the Ministry of Interior’s Civil Status Agency processed an additional 570,520 transactions. The Absher Individuals platform also recorded the issuance of 125,580 reports through its Absher Reports service, alongside 1,799 general inquiries related to fingerprinting. The unified digital identities issued through the Absher platform enable beneficiaries to access the services of the Ministry of Interior’s various sectors conveniently and reliably through the Absher Individuals, Absher Business, and Absher Government platforms. They also provide access to services offered by government and private entities through the National Unified Access Portal (Nafath).

items.title: GCC media ministers vow tougher media oversight, accountability for violations
items.title_zh: 海湾合作委员会媒体部长誓言加强媒体监督，对违规行为追究责任
items.summary: MANAMA — Ministers of media and information of the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries have called for tighter media surveillance and systematic documentation of violations across media outlets and digital platforms. In a joint statement issued at the end of their 29th session in Manama on Wednesday, the ministers stressed the need for decisive legal action to ensure that offenders are held accountable by the competent authorities in each country. “This will be carried out through the application of national regulations and the relevant Gulf decisions and regulations approved by the GCC states, in accordance with the procedures followed in each state,” they said. Saudi Minister of Media Salman Al-Dossary and ministers of media from other Gulf countries attended the meeting. The Gulf ministers underlined their categorical rejection of anything that aims to undermine Gulf unity or offend the GCC states, their symbols, and their peoples. The ministers underscored that the cohesion and solidarity among the GCC states, their leaderships, and their peoples represent a robust pillar for protecting security and stability and safeguarding Gulf achievements. They stressed that Gulf unity is a shared responsibility and a steadfast commitment among the GCC states, the significance of which increases in light of current circumstances to confront challenges and their repercussions. The ministers called on media institutions, media professionals, and users of social media platforms to adhere to their responsibilities, ensure accuracy, and obtain information from official sources, while avoiding the publication or circulation of offensive or misleading content. They emphasized that the sensitive nature of the current phase necessitates concerted efforts to safeguard Gulf unity, solidify fraternal ties among the peoples of the GCC states, and support all that fortifies their security and stability.

items.title: Saudi, Kuwaiti foreign ministers discuss efforts for regional de-escalation
items.title_zh: 沙特、科威特外长讨论地区降级努力
items.summary: RIYADH — Saudi Minister of Foreign Affairs Prince Faisal bin Farhan received Minister of Foreign Affairs of Kuwait Sheikh Jarrah Jaber Al-Ahmad Al-Sabah in Riyadh on Wednesday. During the meeting, the ministers reviewed the well-established fraternal relations between the two countries and ways to further enhance bilateral cooperation across various fields. Prince Faisal and Sheikh Jarrah discussed the latest developments in the region, as well as efforts to de-escalate and contain tensions to help restore regional security and stability. The ministers condemned the terrorist Houthi militia's attacks on Saudi Arabia. They underscored the solidarity of their nations in confronting any threats to their security and stability.

items.title: FII PRIORITY Compass: Cost of living tops global concerns for 5th straight year as financial strains derail family aspirations
items.title_zh: FII PRIORITY COMPASS ：由于财务压力破坏了家庭愿望，生活成本连续第五年成为全球关注的焦点
items.summary: RIYADH — The findings of the fifth edition of the FII PRIORITY Compass underscore the mounting cost-of-living crisis as the foremost concern worldwide, followed by poverty, inequality, and unemployment. The results highlight the deepening grip of financial pressures on everyday decisions, household priorities, and families’ aspirations for the future. The Future Investment Initiative (FII) Institute, a global nonprofit foundation with an investment arm and one agenda, Impact on Humanity, published the findings on Wednesday. The FII PRIORITY Compass captured the views of 61,200 adults across 32 countries, highlighting economic pressures, expectations of technology, and shifting public trust. CEO of FII Institute Princess Dr. Maha bint Mishari bin Abdulaziz said: “The FII PRIORITY Compass reveals shared concerns and unmet needs, with cost-of-living topping global priorities for five years. It should be a go-to resource for investors and decision-makers, guiding policies and capital toward opportunities that generate returns and improve lives.” The compass also reveals a significant gap in outlook between the Global South and the Global North. While 47 percent of respondents in the Global South believe the world is heading in the right direction, only 15 percent in the Global North share that view. On artificial intelligence, the responses reflect a growing recognition of its benefits alongside widespread calls for regulation. While 60 percent said AI has improved their lives, 85 percent call for global rules to regulate its use. This variation also extends to the acceptance of robots in the home, with 61 percent of respondents expressing comfort with robots performing household tasks, compared with 53 percent when it comes to caring for the elderly.Regarding children's safety in the digital environment, 51 percent support requiring verified parental consent for children under the age of 16 to use social media platforms, while 40 percent support banning children's accounts. The survey also highlights the relationship between financial pressures and family decisions, with 57 percent of respondents reporting that living expenses and debt represent barriers to having the number of children they desire.On media and public trust, findings show that a majority of respondents trust traditional media as sources of accurate information, despite 75 percentperceiving them as politically biased. Conducted in partnership with Ipsos between April 24 and June 5, 2026, the online survey gathered views from 61,200 adults aged 18 and over in 32 countries, collectively representing 66 percent of the global population.

items.title: Saudi Arabia recalls 6,388 Mercedes-Benz vehicles over brake failure risk
items.title_zh: 沙特阿拉伯因刹车故障风险召回6,388辆梅赛德斯-奔驰汽车
items.summary: RIYADH — Saudi Arabia’s Ministry of Commerce has recalled 6,388 Mercedes-Benz S-Class and S-Class Maybach vehicles over a brake hose defect that could reduce braking efficiency. The recall covers S-Class and S-Class Maybach vehicles from model years 2020 to 2025. According to the ministry, the defect involves the front axle brake hoses, which could develop brake fluid leaks over time, reducing braking efficiency and increasing stopping distances and the risk of an accident. Owners of affected vehicles are advised to check whether their Vehicle Identification Number (VIN) is included in the recall through Recalls.sa. The ministry urged affected owners to contact Ibrahim Al-Juffali Automotive Company at 8002443000 to arrange the necessary repairs free of charge.

items.title: Urdu, Bengali, Indonesian among 7 languages added to GOSI website and app
items.title_zh: 乌尔都语、孟加拉语、印度尼西亚语等7种语言被添加到GOSI网站和应用程序中
items.summary: RIYADH — The General Organization for Social Insurance (GOSI) has announced the addition of seven new languages to its website and GOSI app as part of its efforts to help customers, who do not speak Arabic or English, better access its digital services.The new languages are Urdu, Bengali, Filipino, Hindi, Sinhala, Nepali, and Indonesian. The move aims to provide a more user-friendly digital experience for speakers of these languages, as well as to enable them to browse its platforms and understand their insurance rights and obligations in their mother tongues. It will also facilitate the completion of related procedures and requests.
